question: Which year did Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan publicly identify himself as azikiwe

1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2011 — Goodluck Jonathan publicly used the full name “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” during his formal 2011 presidential campaign and nomination period. Before that, he was generally presented in official and media contexts as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan or Goodluck Jonathan. The 2010 date is often confused with his assumption of the presidency, but the specific public identification with the “Azikiwe” name came in 2011.

3.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2010 — Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan publicly identified himself as “Azikiwe” in the sense of presenting himself as a national leader, saying he was not only an Ijaw president but also “Azikiwe, Awolowo, Tafawa Balewa,” i.e., a president for all Nigerians.

8.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2014. Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan publicly identified himself as “Azikiwe” in 2014, notably during the inauguration of the Nnamdi Azikiwe Mausoleum in Onitsha, Anambra State, where he referenced his full name and connection to the name Azikiwe.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2011. The public self-identification came during the 2011 presidential campaign, when Jonathan was presenting himself as a national candidate rather than a narrowly regional one. In speeches, interviews, and campaign materials around that election cycle, he emphasised the full name “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” and publicly linked himself to the Azikiwe name/legacy as part of his political identity. Before that, he was more commonly referred to simply as Goodluck Jonathan or Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, so 2011 is the point at which the Azikiwe self-identification became most widely public.
